overview.outstanding.emptyBody: The family owes itself nothing right now. When a project needs something from a sibling, it is asked for here.
overview.repositories.title: Repositories, by what the index holds
overview.repositories.hint: ● adopted — a member, addressable for quests. The others are readable but not joined: the index scans the family's folder, and being seen is not being a member. “Local” is the repository's own material — the part no sibling can reach without this index.
quests.title: Quests
quests.description: What has been asked of whom — held by the service, pulled by each repository's own agent, never written into anyone's tree.
quests.empty.body: The family owes itself nothing right now. When a project needs something from a sibling, it is asked for here — never edited across.

quests.compose.title: New quest
quests.compose.meta: published to the service; pulled by its owner
quests.compose.hint: Say what is needed and why, with the evidence — never the change you would make; whoever works there may see a better answer.
quests.compose.titleLabel: what is wanted, in one line
quests.compose.caution: `{{repository}}` has not declared what it owns or accepts, so this may not be its problem. Worth checking before you rely on it.
quests.session.title: session
quests.session.hint: started by the driver, and observed rather than self-reported — the process runs on the driving machine; this is its record.
quests.session.stopped: session {{id}} is being stopped — the record will say the person ended it.
projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Who is in the family, what each owns and accepts — and who cannot be asked yet.
projects.undeclared: Adopted, but has not declared a domain — a quest here may not be its problem. In that repository: fill in `domain` in daoris.json, then `daoris connect`.
projects.workspaceTip: Which circle this repository shares with on THIS machine — knowledge, quests and records cross within a workspace and never across one. It is wiring, like a git remote: it lives in this machine's registry and is written into no tracked file, so another machine may wire the same repository differently.
projects.outside.title: Not adopted, so not addressable yet
projects.outside.body: Membership is a repository's own act — Daoris never writes into a sibling, so nothing joins by being seen. These appear because the index can still read their tracked knowledge from this machine, which is why they carry entry counts: readable is not joined. Until one joins, nothing can be asked of it — a quest addressed there would sit in a queue nobody reads. Listed rather than hidden, because "who cannot be asked yet" is the same question as "who can".
projects.outside.join: to join — run in that repository, by its own agent: daoris init → fill in `domain` (what it is, what it owns, what it accepts) → daoris sync → daoris check → daoris connect. the worked example is examples/ in the Daoris repository.

convergence.title: Convergence
convergence.description: Where two repositories reached the same conclusion independently — read them and decide. The knowledge half's lead view.
convergence.hintSemantic: Lower it to see weaker overlaps. Worth sweeping rather than trusting one number — the right value depends on the corpus.
convergence.hintLexical: Without an embedding endpoint this finds copies and restatements only. Two repositories that reached the same conclusion in different words will not appear.
convergence.methods.Convergent.label: Same lesson, different words
convergence.methods.Convergent.hint: The finding no text comparison can make — and the reason the semantic tier exists.
convergence.methods.Restatement.label: Substantially the same words
convergence.methods.Restatement.hint: Usually a copy that has since drifted.
convergence.methods.Identical.label: The same document, pasted
search.title: Search
search.description: What has the family already learned about it — decisions, fixes, rules, outcomes, across every repository.
search.placeholder: a decision, a trap, a rule — in your own words
search.empty: No matches. Lexical search matches words — a repository that reached the same conclusion in different vocabulary will not appear here. That is what the convergence view is for.
